entries.a: Water boils at a hundred degrees Celsius, two hundred and twelve Fahrenheit, at sea level.
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, thirty two Fahrenheit.
Absolute zero is minus two hundred and seventy three point one five degrees Celsius, the coldest anything can possibly be.
Gravity is the force that pulls objects with mass towards each other. It's why you stay on the ground and why planets orbit stars.
Sound travels at about three hundred and forty three metres per second in air.
An atom is the tiny building block of matter, made of protons and neutrons in a nucleus with electrons around it.
DNA is the molecule that carries the instructions for building and running a living thing.
Photosynthesis is how plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food, giving out oxygen.
Oxygen is the gas we need to breathe. It makes up about a fifth of the air.
Air is about seventy eight percent nitrogen and twenty one percent oxygen, with a little argon and other gases.
Water is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, H two O.
The periodic table lists all the known chemical elements in order of atomic number. There are a hundred and eighteen.
Hydrogen is the lightest element, and the most common in the universe.
Diamond is the hardest natural material.
Diamond is pure carbon with its atoms arranged in a very strong crystal structure.
Electricity is the flow of electric charge, usually electrons moving through a wire.
A magnet is something that creates a magnetic field, which pulls on iron and a few other metals.
Energy is the ability to do work or make something change. It comes as heat, light, motion, electricity and more.
Sound is vibrations travelling through air, or water, or a solid, that our ears pick up.
A rainbow is sunlight bent and split into colours by raindrops.
Lightning is a huge spark of static electricity between clouds, or between a cloud and the ground.
Earthquakes happen when blocks of the Earth's crust, called tectonic plates, suddenly slip against each other.
A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust where molten rock, ash and gas can escape.
The blue whale is the biggest animal ever known, up to about thirty metres long.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal, over three hundred kilometres an hour in a dive. On land, it's the cheetah, at around a hundred.
The giraffe is the tallest animal, up to about five and a half metres.
The African elephant is the largest land animal.
It's hard to say, but chimpanzees, dolphins, crows and octopuses are all famously clever.
Spiders have eight legs.
Insects have six legs.
An octopus has three hearts.
Elephants live for about sixty to seventy years.
Cats purr when they are content, but also sometimes when they are stressed or hurt, to soothe themselves.
Indoor cats often live fifteen years or more, some into their twenties.
Dogs usually live ten to fifteen years, with small breeds living longer than big ones.
No, dolphins are mammals. They breathe air and feed their young milk.
Botanically a tomato is a fruit, though cooks treat it as a vegetable.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest, covering about a third of the planet.
There are five named oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.
There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America.
Asia is the largest continent.
Australia is the smallest continent.
The Nile and the Amazon are the two contenders, at roughly six and a half thousand kilometres each. The Nile is traditionally named the longest.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, at 8,849 metres.
The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest place in the ocean, nearly eleven kilometres down.
Antarctica is technically the largest desert, and the Sahara is the largest hot desert.
Russia is the largest country by area.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building, at about eight hundred and twenty eight metres.
An adult human has two hundred and six bones.
Adults normally have thirty two teeth, including the wisdom teeth.
Humans have forty six chromosomes, in twenty three pairs.
The human heart has four chambers.
Your skin is the biggest organ of the human body.
About sixty percent of an adult human body is water.
Most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep a night. And you, Commander, probably need more than you get.
Normal human body temperature is around thirty seven degrees Celsius, ninety eight point six Fahrenheit.
The classic answer is five: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. Scientists count more, such as balance.
Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter: three point one four one five nine, and it goes on forever.
A prime number can only be divided by one and itself. Two, three, five, seven, eleven and so on.
A triangle has three sides.
A hexagon has six sides.
A circle has three hundred and sixty degrees.
The angles of a triangle add up to a hundred and eighty degrees.
The square root of a hundred is ten.
A rainbow has seven colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
